title: Amazon return and refund request via uploaded audio
hard_category_focus: Amazon order history lookup for refund
breadth_reason: This script extends breadth by testing the full pipeline from uploaded audio ASR through real Amazon signed-in surface verification, including decline if surface is not visible.

v7_target.engine: user-device engine installed via public download
v7_target.surface_rule: Amazon.com signed-in Chrome profile with order history page visible
v7_target.proof_rule: Fresh screenshot of Amazon order page showing order details and signed-in user, captured by the user-device engine

primary_user_input.reason: Using uploaded audio ASR ensures the system handles real speech input from a file, covering a key use case where users provide audio recordings rather than live dictation.

real_user_surfaces.name: Amazon signed-in Chrome
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: screenshot showing Amazon user menu with email/name

real_user_surfaces.name: Amazon order history page
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: screenshot of order history page with list of orders

moments.description: User navigates to https://www.anticipy.ai/app and signs in, completes onboarding, and downloads the public installer.
Driver checks that the user has Amazon.com open in a Chrome tab with their signed-in profile and order history page accessible.

moments.spoken_reference_text: On the Amazon order page for the running shoes I bought last month, please check the return window and draft a customer message to support to refund the order. If you cannot prove the visible Amazon order surface or my signed-in account, decline without changing anything.
moments.delivery_instruction: The stranger will upload an MP3 audio file via /api/listen/upload containing the spoken reference text.

moments.description: Engine verifies that the ASR transcript corresponds to the current live Amazon surface and that no stale or fake data is used.
Engine decides whether to act (draft refund request), ask (for clarification), or decline (if surface not verifiable).
Driver observes that the primary input mode is audio upload and notes that other modes (transcript paste, live mic) are not primary, but still visible as options.

success_criteria: User successfully uploads an MP3 audio file.
ASR produces accurate transcript matching the spoken reference text.
Engine matches the request to the Amazon order history page visible in the user's signed-in Chrome.
Engine either drafts a refund message or properly declines if surface is not verifiable.
All proofs are fresh and sourced from the public build.
failure_triggers: If the user does not have Amazon signed-in in Chrome, the engine must decline.
If ASR fails to transcribe the audio, the engine must not proceed.
If the surface is not the real user's profile, the engine must decline.
If the engine attempts to bypass surface verification, that is a failure.
If the proof uses stale or fake data, it fails.
